subject.title: EPERM crashes on database files during active locks in applyPrivateModeSync

question: How should shared-state SQLite permission hardening handle EPERM on live WAL/SHM sidecars when the parent state directory is private but the sidecar mode is still broad?
rationale: The availability fix is plausible, but the same helper protects credentials-adjacent state permissions and prior maintainer follow-up intentionally kept ordinary EPERM failures fatal.

options.title: Scope tolerance to live shared-state sidecars
options.body: Tolerate or defer EPERM only for shared-state SQLite sidecars under a private state directory, log the degraded hardening, and keep directory/main-file ownership failures fatal.

options.title: Require real lock proof first
options.body: Ask for a concrete active-lock reproduction or platform log before changing the current fail-closed EPERM policy.

options.title: Keep fail-closed policy unchanged
options.body: Treat unresolved EPERM on broad-mode database files as a hard security boundary and close only if maintainers decide availability should not override hardening here.

recommendation.title: Scope tolerance to live shared-state sidecars
recommendation.body: Tolerate or defer EPERM only for shared-state SQLite sidecars under a private state directory, log the degraded hardening, and keep directory/main-file ownership failures fatal.
